summary: Master indigenous social protection using ILO 169 and UNDRIP. Learn culturally safe design, FPIC protocols, and data sovereignty. Enroll for expert training.
lede: Social protection for Indigenous populations involves designing programmes that reach people fairly and respect collective rights. For social protection managers, policy advisers, and Indigenous affairs specialists, the course supports practical work to assess coverage gaps, adapt registration and payment pathways, and develop monitoring and grievance processes that account for accessibility and Indigenous participation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape, manage, evaluate, or support social protection programmes affecting Indigenous populations. It suits intermediate practitioners who can relate the tools to an existing programme, policy portfolio, or service-delivery challenge.
outcomes: Free Prior Informed Consent Protocol Design
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to social protection policy, social assistance delivery, Indigenous affairs, development programming, monitoring and evaluation, or related public service operations. No programming experience is required. Bring a current programme concept, policy challenge, or anonymized delivery example if available.
